variants.title: Follow a publish
variants.context: In AMQP 0-9-1, a publisher targets an exchange with a routing key; the exchange evaluates bindings and sends a copy to each matching queue; the queue stores the copy and dispatches deliveries; the consumer commits the effect and acknowledges.
variants.prompt: A service publishes generate.invoice. Put the broker path in order.

items.text: The publisher serializes a versioned message with a stable ID and selects exchange and routing key.
The exchange evaluates bindings; zero, one, or many queues match.
Each matching queue stores its copy per queue type, persistence, and replication.
A consumer commits the business operation, then acknowledges, negatively acknowledges, or rejects.

variants.hint: Publishers do not target queues directly.
variants.explanation: Publisher → exchange → queue copy → consumer. Declared bindings decide which queues receive independent copies.

variants.title: Follow a publish
variants.context: In AMQP 0-9-1, a publisher targets an exchange with a routing key; the exchange evaluates bindings and sends a copy to each matching queue; the queue stores the copy and dispatches deliveries; the consumer commits the effect and acknowledges.
variants.prompt: A mandatory publish matches nothing. Put the steps in order.

items.text: The publisher sends with the mandatory flag.
The exchange evaluates bindings and finds no match.
The broker returns the message to the publisher instead of storing it.
The publisher treats the return as a routing failure and alerts.

variants.hint: A return is a protocol-level signal of an unroutable publish.
variants.explanation: Enable mandatory publishing when unroutable messages are failures; alert on returns.

variants.title: Follow a publish
variants.context: In AMQP 0-9-1, a publisher targets an exchange with a routing key; the exchange evaluates bindings and sends a copy to each matching queue; the queue stores the copy and dispatches deliveries; the consumer commits the effect and acknowledges.
variants.prompt: Two queues are bound to the same topic pattern. Put the steps in order.

items.text: The publisher sends one message to the exchange.
The exchange finds both bindings match.
Each queue stores its own copy.
Each queue’s consumer processes and acknowledges independently.

variants.explanation: A consumer acknowledgement never proves what another queue’s consumer did.

variants.title: Choose the exchange
variants.context: Direct exchanges match an exact key; topic exchanges match dot-separated words where * is exactly one word and # is zero or more; fanout copies to every bound queue; headers match attributes.
variants.prompt: Every event has one stable category such as payment.failed.us and consumers want exact matches. Which exchange?
optionFeedback: A binding key must equal the routing key.
Fanout ignores the key and copies everywhere.
Headers work but are harder to discover and operate.
variants.hint: Is the match exact, a pattern, or everything?
variants.explanation: Direct exchanges fit stable, exact categories.

variants.title: Choose the exchange
variants.context: Direct exchanges match an exact key; topic exchanges match dot-separated words where * is exactly one word and # is zero or more; fanout copies to every bound queue; headers match attributes.
variants.prompt: Consumers want patterns such as orders.*.eu across a bounded vocabulary. Which exchange?
optionFeedback: Topic bindings match dot-separated words with * and #.
Direct needs an exact key per binding.
Fanout cannot filter.
variants.explanation: Use stable semantic words in keys, not table names.

variants.title: Choose the exchange
variants.context: Direct exchanges match an exact key; topic exchanges match dot-separated words where * is exactly one word and # is zero or more; fanout copies to every bound queue; headers match attributes.
variants.prompt: All current subscribers must intentionally receive every publish, key ignored. Which exchange?
options: Topic with a single exact key.
optionFeedback: Every bound queue receives a copy.
Direct filters by key.
A topic with one key is a roundabout direct.
variants.explanation: Fanout is broadcast; accidental fanout is a routing bug worth alerting on.

variants.title: Name the evidence
variants.context: A successful publish, a routed queue copy, a consumer delivery, and a completed business effect are four different facts. Publisher confirms cover broker acceptance; consumer acknowledgements cover delivery completion; mandatory publishes are returned when no queue matches.
variants.prompt: The publisher received a confirm. Has any consumer processed the message?
options: Not necessarily. A confirm covers broker acceptance, not consumer receipt.
Yes, if the queue is durable.
optionFeedback: A confirm can arrive before any consumer sees the message.
Confirms and consumer acks are separate facts.
Durability does not imply consumption.
variants.hint: Which boundary did the confirm cover?
variants.explanation: Design and observe each of the four boundaries separately.

variants.title: Name the evidence
variants.context: A successful publish, a routed queue copy, a consumer delivery, and a completed business effect are four different facts. Publisher confirms cover broker acceptance; consumer acknowledgements cover delivery completion; mandatory publishes are returned when no queue matches.
variants.prompt: A consumer’s channel closes while a delivery is unacknowledged. What does the broker do?
options: It can redeliver the message to another consumer.
optionFeedback: Unacknowledged deliveries are owned attempts the broker can redeliver.
Unacknowledged work is not lost.
Only an acknowledgement completes the delivery.
variants.explanation: Consumers must be duplicate-safe because redelivery after a channel loss is normal.

variants.title: Name the evidence
variants.context: A successful publish, a routed queue copy, a consumer delivery, and a completed business effect are four different facts. Publisher confirms cover broker acceptance; consumer acknowledgements cover delivery completion; mandatory publishes are returned when no queue matches.
variants.prompt: A consumer acknowledged in queue A. Does that tell you what queue B’s consumer did with its copy?
options: No. An acknowledgement is per delivery per queue.
Yes, if both queues share the exchange.
optionFeedback: Each queue copy has its own delivery and acknowledgement.
Acks are scoped to one delivery.
The exchange only routed copies.
variants.explanation: Publisher confirms are not consumer receipts, and one queue’s ack says nothing about another queue.

variants.title: Make durability complete
variants.context: Quorum queues are a Raft-based replicated log; a majority of members must be available for progress. Use an odd replica count across independent failure domains. A multi-node cluster does not make a queue highly available by itself.
variants.prompt: A new replicated, durable work queue is needed. Which type?
options: A quorum queue with an odd replica count across failure domains.
A classic queue on one node.
Any queue, since the cluster has three nodes.
optionFeedback: Quorum queues replicate via Raft and need a majority to progress.
Classic single-node queues fit transient workloads.
Node count alone does not replicate a queue.
variants.hint: What decides a queue’s data path?
variants.explanation: Do not call a queue highly available merely because the cluster has several nodes.

variants.title: Make durability complete
variants.context: Quorum queues are a Raft-based replicated log; a majority of members must be available for progress. Use an odd replica count across independent failure domains. A multi-node cluster does not make a queue highly available by itself.
variants.prompt: A quorum queue has three members and one node is lost. Can the queue make progress?
options: Yes; two of three is a majority.
optionFeedback: Majority availability is the Raft rule.
A majority, not all, is required.
Progress covers publishes and deliveries.
variants.hint: How many of three form a majority?
variants.explanation: Odd replica counts across independent failure domains keep majorities meaningful.

variants.title: Make durability complete
variants.context: Quorum queues are a Raft-based replicated log; a majority of members must be available for progress. Use an odd replica count across independent failure domains. A multi-node cluster does not make a queue highly available by itself.
variants.prompt: All quorum-queue leaders ended up on one node. What is the risk?
options: One node owns every hot path; losing it disrupts everything at once.
optionFeedback: Keep queue leaders distributed.
Leaders coordinate the replicated log.
Concentration is a failure-domain problem.
variants.hint: Where does the write path run?
variants.explanation: Test node and zone loss while publishers wait for confirms.

variants.title: Count the matches
variants.context: Direct exchanges match an exact key; topic exchanges match dot-separated words where * is exactly one word and # is zero or more; fanout copies to every bound queue; headers match attributes.
variants.prompt: Routing keys: orders.created.eu, orders.created.us, orders.shipped.eu, payments.failed.eu. How many match the binding orders.*.eu?
variants.explanation: orders.created.eu and orders.shipped.eu match; the us key and the payments key do not.

mistakes.feedback: orders.created.us ends in us, not eu.
Both created and shipped in eu match.

variants.title: Count the matches
variants.context: Direct exchanges match an exact key; topic exchanges match dot-separated words where * is exactly one word and # is zero or more; fanout copies to every bound queue; headers match attributes.
variants.prompt: Same four keys. How many match the binding orders.#?
variants.explanation: All three orders.* keys match; payments.failed.eu does not.

mistakes.feedback: payments.failed.eu does not start with orders.
# matches any number of trailing words.

variants.title: Count the matches

variants.prompt: Same four keys. How many match the binding #.eu?
variants.explanation: orders.created.eu, orders.shipped.eu, and payments.failed.eu match; the us key does not.
